title: Introduction to Python Data Structures
overview: Data structures are ways to organize and store data efficiently. Python provides built-in structures like lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries.

title: Lists in Python
overview: Lists are ordered and mutable collections that can store multiple values of different data types.

title: List Methods
overview: Python lists provide built-in methods to add, remove, sort, and modify elements.

title: Tuples in Python
overview: Tuples are ordered collections similar to lists but they are immutable, meaning their values cannot be changed after creation.

title: Sets in Python
overview: Sets are unordered collections that store unique values. They are useful for removing duplicate data.

title: Dictionaries in Python
overview: Dictionaries store data in key-value pairs. They are commonly used for structured data.

title: Nested Data Structures
overview: Python allows combining data structures together, such as lists inside dictionaries or dictionaries inside lists.

title: Choosing the Right Data Structure
overview: Different data structures are useful for different situations depending on whether you need ordering, uniqueness, or key-based access.

example.title: Selection Guide
example.content:
List → Ordered data
Tuple → Fixed data
Set → Unique values
Dictionary → Key-value data

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned Python's main data structures including lists, tuples, sets, dictionaries, their features, and when to use them.
